newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: LEHMAN, CT SMITH IN S.LANKA INVESTMENT PROMOTION.
newsitem.headline: LEHMAN, CT SMITH IN S.LANKA INVESTMENT PROMOTION.

text.p: Lehman Brothers and Sri Lankan brokerage CT Smith began a two-day meeting of fund managers on Thursday to promote investments in the Indian Ocean island.
More than 15 local and foreign fund managers will meet Sri Lankan government and business officials at the "Riding the Recovery" conference.
The stock market index, which closed at 850.7 points on Wednesday after gaining over 200 points this year, is expected to gain further steam along with the economy.
Growth in Sri Lanka's gross domestic product fell to 3.8 percent in 1996 from 5.5 in 1995 due to a severe drought which hit power supply, industry and agriculture.

Tourism and investor sentiment also slumped after Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam rebels, fighting for a separate homeland in Sri Lanka's north and east, bombed the Central Bank and a crowded commuter train last year.
The Central Bank says GDP growth should rise to six percent in 1996.
